reason: E2 shows that 0.25 wt % Y2O3 in CrMnFeCoNi improves room-temperature wear resistance without affecting friction, but provides no evidence for high-temperature glaze formation or friction reduction. E1 demonstrates adaptive glaze layers and ultralow wear in a different alloy (Ni50(AlNbTiV)50) without Y2O3, so it does not support the claim that Y2O3 nanoparticles catalyze such layers in CoCrFeNi. The key premises about high-temperature mechanisms and full-range performance are therefore unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Y2O3 nanoparticles can be uniformly dispersed in a CoCrFeNi matrix at 0.25–0.5 wt %
Y2O3 nanoparticles will reinforce the alloy at room temperature by impeding dislocations and reducing friction
Y2O3 nanoparticles will catalyze tribochemical reactions to form a lubricious glaze layer at high temperatures
The glaze layer will minimize adhesive and oxidative wear from RT to 800 °C
The intervention will yield 1–2 orders of magnitude lower wear rate across the full temperature range
